children: Bulgaria on Wednesday approved lifting a ban on fuel exports to other EU countries that has been in place since last year to protect domestic supplies after US sanctions targeted Russia's Lukoil, operator of the country's biggest oil refinery.
The measure was approved by parliament by 121 votes to 42, with 23 lawmakers abstaining.
The government has said the ban, mainly on diesel and aviation fuel, hit the activities of Lukoil's

refinery and posed significant administrative and organisational difficulties for fuel businesses, causing financial losses for some operators which failed to meet contractual obligations to international partners.
It also said the ban went against the free movement of goods principle of the EU single market.
Lukoil runs Bulgaria's 190,000-barrel-per-day Burgas oil refinery, operates more than 200 petrol stations and has a fuel transport and depot network.
